literal: Virtue, wealth, pleasure, and fear for life—of these four, having examined the nature, (a person) is to be trusted.
translation: A person should be chosen and trusted only after testing them through the fourfold trials of virtue, wealth, pleasure, and the fear of losing one's life.
modern: அறம், பொருள், இன்பம், உயிர் மேல் உள்ள பயம் ஆகிய நான்கு வழிகளிலும் ஒருவருடைய குணத்தை ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்த பிறகே அவரைத் தேர்ந்தெடுக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential tests to evaluate a person's character before employing them in a position of trust. The tests examine how the person responds to the pull of virtue (அறம்), the temptation of wealth (பொருள்), the desire for pleasure (இன்பம்), and the instinct of self-preservation or fear of death (உயிரச்சம்). By observing their behavior under these four pressures, their true nature (திறம்) is revealed. Only those who remain steadfast and upright through all four trials should be trusted (தேறப்படும்) with responsibility.
